facts.text: Co was systematically substituted for Ni in Mn0.6Ni1−xSi0.62Fe0.4CoxGe0.38 by varying x from 0.40 to 0.55.
The alloys were annealed at 750 °C for 72 h in high vacuum and then water-quenched.
DSC measurements were conducted from 183 to 400 K at 10 K min−1 under N2.
Magnetic entropy changes were derived from isothermal magnetization measurements near TC using fields up to 5 T.
Increasing Co content stabilized the hexagonal Ni2In-type austenite and shifted its transformation to orthorhombic TiNiSi-type martensite to lower temperature.
The x = 0.40–0.50 alloys underwent coupled first-order magnetostructural transitions, whereas x = 0.55 exhibited a second-order magnetic transition.

The giant magnetocaloric response arose when ferromagnetic TiNiSi-type martensite and paramagnetic Ni2In-type austenite transformed near the Curie temperature; loss of this coupling at x = 0.55 produced a small response.

Relative to x = 0.40, increasing Co lowered the structural-transition and Curie temperatures and progressively reduced the peak magnetic entropy change, suppressing the giant first-order response at x = 0.55.
The structural-transition temperature decreased from 306 K at x = 0.40 to 286 K at x = 0.45 and 269 K at x = 0.50; no DSC peak for x = 0.55 appeared between 183 and 400 K.
At 5 T, the peak −ΔSM values were 48.5, 42.9, 31.7, and 2.6 J kg−1 K−1 for x = 0.40, 0.45, 0.50, and 0.55, respectively.
For x = 0.40 near 306.5 K, direct ΔTad reached 8.2 K under a 5 T superconducting field and 14.1 K under a 4.8 T pulsed field.
Hardness increased from 552 HV2 at x = 0.40 to 758 HV2 at x = 0.55, and x = 0.55 had the highest reported compressive strength of 267 MPa.
